Situation Report 
Chad Humanitarian Response 
1-31 May 2026
Highlights 
● Refugee arrivals from Sudan slow amid border insecurity: By 30 May 2026, a total of
928,818 refugees had arrived from Sudan since April 2023, with Ouaddaï hosting the largest
number.1 Arrivals declined in May, likely due to increased border insecurity, including a 26
May drone strike in Al-Tina.2
● Insecurity and funding shortfalls increase protection risks in Lac: In Lac Province,
non-state armed group (NSAG) attacks on 4 and 6 May triggered new displacements and a
state of emergency. Funding gaps have also forced humanitarian actors to scale back
services, limiting access to sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and protection services. A
security audit across 25 sites revealed that 96% of sites lacked night lighting and 68%
lacked latrines, heightening gender-based violence (GBV) risks.
● Intercommunal tensions restrict access to essential services in Wadi Fira: Tensions
between the Zaghawa and Tama communities persist in Wadi-Fira Province, with clashes in
Birak and Marassabré resulting in casualties. The violence undermines social cohesion,
restricts population movement, and hinders access to SRH and GBV services.
● Senior UNFPA leadership visits Chad: A high-level UNFPA mission visited N’Djamena,
Ouaddaï, and Wadi-Fira to engage with government authorities, assess humanitarian needs,
convene donor meetings, and review ongoing interventions.
● 90% funding gap: As of May 2026, UNFPA has only received 10% of funding it requires for
Chad, severely restricting life-saving SRH and GBV services for vulnerable women and girls.

bullets: CHAPTER II MEMBERSHIP Article 3 The original Members of the United Nations shall be the states which, having participated in the United Nations Conference on International Organization at San Francisco, or having previ- ously signed the Declaration by United Nations of January 1,1942, sign the present Charter and ratify it in accordance with Article 110.

Article 5 / A Member of the United Nations against which preventive or enforcement action has been taken by the Security Council may be suspended from the exercise of the rights and privileges of mem- bership by the General Assembly upon the recom- mendation of the Security Council.

Article 6 A Member of the United Nations which has persistently violated the Principles contained in the present Charter may be expelled from the Organization by the General Assembly upon the recommendation of the Security Council.

Accordingly, our respective Governments, through representatives assembled in the city of San Francisco, who have exhibited their full powers found to be in good and due form, have agreed to the present Charter of the United Nations and do hereby establish an international organization to be known as the United Nations.

The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps warned ships not to approach the strategic waterway, which before the war carried a fifth of global oil and liquid gas supplies, citing what it called Israeli crimes in Lebanon and a US violation of commitments to establish a ceasefire there.
Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon on Saturday killed at least 16 people, local authorities said, despite reports of a renewed ceasefire aiming to end the continuing clashes.

related.title: US-Iran talks in Switzerland: Is Lebanon top of agenda; who is attending?
related.summary: “Here, they [Iran] are talking particularly about … the cessation of hostilities in Lebanon, the lifting of the US maritime blockade, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, the release of Iranian frozen assets and, of course, the lifting of US sanctions when it comes to Iran’s oil sector and petrochemical products and related sectors,” he said.
bullets: “Here, they [Iran] are talking particularly about … the cessation of hostilities in Lebanon, the lifting of the US maritime blockade, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, the release of Iranian frozen assets and, of course, the lifting of US sanctions when it comes to Iran’s oil sector and petrochemical products and related sectors,” he said.

Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and army chief Asim Munir, as well as Qatar’s Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, are also expected to take part in the talks, as Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced they were closing the Strait of Hormuz over ceasefire violations in Lebanon.

The technical talks between the US and Iran will take place for 60 days, where officials from both sides are expected to discuss the final phase of the peace process and find solutions to resolve major sticking points, such as Iran’s nuclear programme and Israel’s war on Lebanon.
Before departing for the talks on Saturday, Vance told reporters in the US that he hopes to make “progress on the nuclear issue” and “on the Lebanon ceasefire issue”.

United States and Iranian delegations are gearing up for high-level technical talks slated to be held in Switzerland, as a deal signed on Thursday between Tehran and Washington is strained by continued Israeli attacks on Lebanon.

related.title: Vance arrives in Switzerland for US-Iran talks
related.summary: The US and Iran earlier this week agreed to a 60-day ceasefire extension for the negotiations, but Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Saturday announced the closure of the ⁠Strait of Hormuz in response to Israeli attacks in Lebanon – although the US military said commercial vessels kept operating. Trump said no toll would be charged for passage through the strait during or after the 60-day ceasefire – unless the US imposes one should peace talks fail.
bullets: The US and Iran earlier this week agreed to a 60-day ceasefire extension for the negotiations, but Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) on Saturday announced the closure of the ⁠Strait of Hormuz in response to Israeli attacks in Lebanon – although the US military said commercial vessels kept operating.
